title: Automated Onboarding SLO Escalation & Orchestration Playbook
author: Elena Park
body:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook defines the automated orchestration and escalation process used during enterprise onboarding to ensure SLO-driven stability, fast triage, and consistent customer communication. It applies to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments during the first 90 calendar days after provisioning, with integrations into Alerting, Pager, Ticketing, and Customer Success systems.

Key objectives:
- Detect onboarding-impacting SLO regressions automatically and reduce MTTI (mean time to identify) to under 5 minutes where possible.
- Route incidents to the right team and automation step based on severity and customer tier.
- Ensure customers see timely, transparent updates and have an engineered remediation path.
- Capture telemetry and post-incident signals into onboarding QBRs.

Definitions and SLOs monitored during onboarding:
- Availability (API success rate): target >= 99.8% per customer per 1h window; warning at 99.5%, critical at 99.0%.
- Latency (p95 generation): target <= 350ms; warning at >450ms, critical at >800ms for three consecutive minutes.
- Token error rate: target < 0.2% per model route per 1h; warning at 0.5%, critical at 1.0%.
- Model quality regressions: automated eval failure rate > 5% vs baseline on onboarding prompt set (see "Onboarding Eval Sets" reference).

Alerting and severity mapping (automated rules):
1) SEV-WARN (automated): signaled when a single SLO crosses warning threshold for a rolling 15-minute window OR a single customer sees >2x baseline error rate for 5 minutes.
   - Action: create ticket (CSIN- auto), post to #cs-monitoring channel, run quick mitigation automation (see Automation actions).
2) SEV-1 (automated human escalation): triggered when threshold crosses critical for 3 consecutive minutes OR multiple SLOs cross warning thresholds simultaneously for the same customer.
   - Action: page on-call SRE and CS on-call, open conference bridge, set customer-facing incident status to "investigating".
3) SEV-2 (manual): for partial degradation with single-customer impact where automated mitigation succeeded but risk remains.
   - Action: CS owner initiates outreach and schedules canary rollback if needed.

Automation actions (ordered, idempotent):
- Action A (prefix-cache-warm): replay recent prefixes from leader cache into KV cache for the customer shard. CLI example:
  curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/cache/prime \ 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPS_TOKEN}' \ 
    -d '{"customer_id":"CUST-12345","model_route":"gptx-32k","prefixes":["/templates/checkout","/support/summary"]}'

- Action B (traffic-shift): execute controlled 5% traffic shift to fallback model variant (quantized) with gradual ramp for 10 minutes. Required approvals recorded automatically.

- Action C (node-evacuate): drain GPU node in tenant pool and force reallocation. Only for SEV-1 and after automated health checks.

- Action D (quota-throttle): temporary tenant-level throttling for noisy subqueues for up to 30 minutes.

Escalation orchestration flow (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Monitoring rules detect SLO breach -> alert POSTed to orchestration endpoint (see 'Alert webhook payload' below).
2) Triage automation: Orchestrator evaluates customer tier, active rollout flags, current token spend, and route-specific health.
3) Mitigation attempt: Run ordered automation actions A->B->C as required with checks between each action (automated rollback if action increases error rate).
4) Human handoff: If mitigation fails or SEV-1, orchestrator pages and opens standard incident bridge and updates customer status.
5) Customer comms: CS owner uses template to notify customer; operations provides technical summary and ETA.
6) Post-incident: All telemetry is archived to onboarding incident index and a follow-up RCA and QBR artifact are required within 72 hours if SEV-1.

Alert webhook payload (required fields):
| field | type | description |
|------:|:----:|:------------:|
| alert_id | string | unique alert id (uuid) |
| customer_id | string | customer tenant id |
| route | string | model route name |
| metric | string | metric name (availability/latency/error_rate/quality) |
| value | string | observed value (number encoded as string) |
| threshold | string | threshold value that was crossed |
| window | string | window length e.g. 5m/15m/1h |
| severity | string | warn|critical |

Example payload (JSON text):
{
  "alert_id": "a1f3b2c4-07d5-4cde-a2f3-9b5f2b7e1c22",
  "customer_id": "CUST-12345",
  "route": "gptx-32k/production",
  "metric": "p95_latency_ms",
  "value": "925",
  "threshold": "800",
  "window": "3m",
  "severity": "critical"
}

Routing rules and ownership matrix:
- If customer.tier == enterprise AND (region == eu-west OR vpc_private == true) -> route to: Private Deployments On-call (eng-private-deployments) + CS owner.
- If model_route contains "dedicated" -> route to Eng: Dedicated On-call + CS.
- Otherwise -> Hosted runtime on-call + CS triage.

Escalation templates (customer-facing) - short first message:
Subject: Redwood Inference: Incident affecting your live inference (CUST-12345)
Message: "We detected increased latency affecting your inference routes. Our team is actively investigating and will provide an update within 15 minutes. Impact: intermittent latency spikes for model route gptx-32k. Immediate mitigation steps are in progress. Contact: <customer-success-rep@redwood.com>"

When to initiate canary rollback vs. model-shift:
- Canary rollback recommended when recent model upgrade rollout timestamp < 72h and error patterns match new model signature (increased hallucination / likelihood spike on eval set).
- Model-shift (fallback model) recommended when node-level GPU saturation or quantization variant has historically lower latency in customer-specific traces.

Operational dashboards and queries (examples):
- Onboarding SLO dashboard (single-customer filter): displays availability, p95 latency, token error rate, model-eval-fail-rate across last 1h/6h/24h windows.
- Suggested PromQL snippets:
  - api_success_rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference",customer_id=~"CUST-.*",code=~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference",customer_id=~"CUST-.*"}[5m]))
  - p95_latency_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{job="inference",customer_id="CUST-12345"}[5m])) by (le))

Post-incident tasks and QBR integration:
- Within 24 hours: CS owner records initial impact summary in ticket and notifies customer of next steps.
- Within 72 hours (for SEV-1): Eng and CS deliver RCA that includes: root cause, mitigation timeline, corrective actions, and one action owner for each corrective item.
- Prior to onboarding QBR: Include incident metrics and trending in the onboarding QBR deck (slo breach counts, time to mitigation, any changes to rollout policies).

Operational safety and guardrails:
- Automation actions are guarded by safety checks: each action requires success criteria (reduction in error rate or latency within 10 minutes) or will be automatically rolled back.
- Node-evacuate (Action C) will only run if >= 2 healthy nodes available in the pool and if maintenance_window == false for customer.
- Traffic-shift cannot be applied for customers on strict model-pin contracts without explicit legal waiver.

Ownership and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Elena Park (Customer Success, playbook author).
- Escalation owner (on-call): Eng-SRE rota (see /eng-sre/oncall-rotations).
- Private deployment emergencies: Eng-Private-Deployments on-call + Solutions Engineering.

Appendix A — Automation runbook commands and examples:
- Check tenant health:
  redwoodctl tenant inspect --tenant CUST-12345 --json

- Initiate traffic-shift (example):
  redwoodctl traffic shift --tenant CUST-12345 --from gptx-32k --to gptx-32k-quantized --percent 5 --duration 10m --approve

Appendix B — Common failure modes and quick remediations:
- Symptom: sudden p95 latency spikes for single region. Remediation: run prefix-cache-warm; if no improvement, perform 5% traffic-shift to fallback model.
- Symptom: elevated token error rate after model upgrade. Remediation: initiate canary rollback for the most recent model bundle and open model-eval job for the onboarding prompt set.
